headline_marked: NCP leader Nahid Islam urges [[government to implement July Charter]]
headline: NCP leader Nahid Islam urges government to implement July Charter
summary: National Citizen Party Convener Nahid Islam accused the BNP-led government of betraying the people's mandate and failing to implement key reforms.
details: National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam has accused the BNP-led government of denying the outcome of a referendum and failing to implement the July Charter, claiming people voted for justice and reforms.
Speaking at the 'July March-2026' programme in Gazipur's Kaliganj upazila, Nahid alleged that the government has betrayed the people's mandate.
The NCP leader placed five demands, insisting that referendum results must be implemented to move reforms forward and achieve meaningful change in the country.
Nahid also criticized the government's handling of the power crisis, stating that many areas are experiencing seven to eight hours of daily load shedding despite promises of improvement.
He urged the government to ensure uninterrupted power supply and bring down the rising cost of living, noting that the national budget offered little hope for resolution.
Concerns were raised over the law and order situation, with Nahid alleging that drug trafficking has spread across the country and urging the home ministry to take effective measures.
Regarding border issues, he alleged that Bangladeshi citizens continue to be killed by India's Border Security Force and criticized the government's failure to prevent such incidents.
He further called for justice for those killed during the July Mass Uprising, the establishment of a July Museum, and an end to the harassment of innocent people through false cases.
caption:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) accuses the government of betraying the people's mandate. What are their demands?

National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam has accused the BNP-led government of denying the outcome of a referendum and failing to implement the July Charter, claiming people voted for justice and reforms.

Speaking at the 'July March-2026' programme in Gazipur's Kaliganj upazila, Nahid alleged that the government has betrayed the people's mandate.

The NCP leader placed five demands, insisting that referendum results must be implemented to move reforms forward and achieve meaningful change in the country.

Nahid also criticized the government's handling of the power crisis, stating that many areas are experiencing seven to eight hours of daily load shedding despite promises of improvement.

He urged the government to ensure uninterrupted power supply and bring down the rising cost of living, noting that the national budget offered little hope for resolution.

Concerns were raised over the law and order situation, with Nahid alleging that drug trafficking has spread across the country and urging the home ministry to take effective measures.

Regarding border issues, he alleged that Bangladeshi citizens continue to be killed by India's Border Security Force and criticized the government's failure to prevent such incidents.

He further called for justice for those killed during the July Mass Uprising, the establishment of a July Museum, and an end to the harassment of innocent people through false cases.

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline_marked: Madrasa head [[arrested for torturing student]] with chains
headline: Madrasa head arrested for torturing student with chains
summary: The head of a madrasa has been arrested after reports emerged that he tortured a student by wrapping chains around their legs.
details: A madrasa head has been arrested following allegations of severe torture against a student.
The suspect is accused of wrapping chains around the student's legs as a form of punishment or torture.
Law enforcement agencies took the suspect into custody after the incident came to light.
The authorities are further investigating the case to determine the extent of the abuse and if other students have been such treatment.
